text: An n-by-n real matrix A is diagonalizable if and only if:
choices: A has n linearly independent eigenvectors
explanation: Diagonalizability is precisely the existence of a basis of eigenvectors, i.e. n linearly independent eigenvectors. Symmetry and having n distinct eigenvalues are each sufficient but not necessary (the identity is diagonalizable with a repeated eigenvalue), and invertibility is irrelevant since a singular matrix can still be diagonalizable.
